rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~79%; BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~97%; RBNZ Dec hike ~57% (from ~80%); BoC Dec ~56%; ECB Dec ~86%; BoJ Dec ~80%; RBA easing priced by end-2027
rows.read: Most big central banks still lean toward higher rates, and the Bank of England is set to raise on Thursday. New Zealand’s weak jobs figures cut bets on a December hike there, and Australia’s central bank now looks done. Currencies are moving on hints about the next step, not the hikes already made.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: NZ unemployment 5.7% Q3 (fcst 5.5%), jobs −0.1%; US job openings 7.52M Sep; US ISM services today 9:00 AM CT (fcst 54.8)
rows.read: The US economy keeps surprising on the strong side, but a Democratic Congress is expected to spend less, which could slow it next year. New Zealand’s job market weakened more than expected, a drag on the kiwi. The US services survey today is the next check on American strength.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Euro-area flash CPI Oct today 4:00 AM CT (fcst 4.0%, Sep 3.8%; core fcst 2.5%); Swiss CPI 1.5% Oct; Brent ~$104.6
rows.read: Fuel is still pushing prices up almost everywhere, though oil has eased from its late-October high. This morning’s euro-area figures are the week’s main inflation check, and a hot reading would firm up a December hike by the European Central Bank. Cheaper oil, if it lasts, would ease pressure on central banks across the board.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Asian shares fell as Democrats won the US Senate and headed for the House, with chip and AI stocks hit hardest. This time the dollar was not the safe place: money went to the franc, the yen, gold and US government bonds. Currencies tied to growth, like the Aussie and kiwi, missed out on the dollar’s fall.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$104.6 (+1%), WTI ~$96.8 in Asia; Tuesday settle ~$103.6 (near 4-week low); IRGC claims four tankers hit mines; API crude −5.3M bbl
rows.read: Oil bounced a little after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said tankers hit mines near Hormuz, but it stays well below its late-October high. That leaves exporters like Canada with less support than a month ago and importers like Japan and the euro area with a smaller bill. A peace deal would widen that gap quickly.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: AP: Democrats win the Senate; networks project the House (AP not yet called); Fitch France A+ negative (Oct 30); Canada budget Nov 5, 3:00 PM CT
rows.read: A Democratic Congress is expected to limit President Trump’s spending plans, which takes some support away from the dollar. Debt worries in France still weigh on the euro. Canada presents its federal budget on Thursday, and a big rise in borrowing would weigh on the loonie.
